security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI writes an invalid (unimplemented) SIDN to msdcfg, then reads mip.SEIP, sireg, stopei, hgeip, hgeie, or hstatus.VGEIN, relying on the now-removed guarantee that these return 0 or trap — hardware behavior is UNSPECIFIED after this change
security_spec.summary: PR removes explicit trapping/zeroing guarantees when msdcfg.SIDN is invalid, so unvalidated SIDN writes followed by CSR reads in OpenSBI M-mode may leak stale interrupt-domain state from other domains

findings.finding: OpenSBI does not implement MSDCFG/SIDN CSR handling. No csr_write to msdcfg exists in the codebase, and none of the dependent CSRs (sireg, stopei, hgeip, hgeie, hstatus) are read after any msdcfg write. The MSDCFG CSR is not even defined in include/sbi/riscv_encoding.h. The vulnerability pattern (write invalid SIDN to msdcfg, then read affected CSRs relying on the removed zero/trap guarantee) cannot occur.
findings.snippet: // No MSDCFG/SIDN-related code found in the OpenSBI source tree
